key_insight: Structurally constrained neural softening functions extend pseudo-elastic Mullins models to capture composition-dependent stress softening while enforcing physical admissibility.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve constitutive predictions for rubber components whose nonlinear response changes with material formulation and loading history.
method: Embed parameter-dependent neural softening functions in a pseudo-elastic framework.
Use a multiplicative decomposition to satisfy common constitutive conditions by construction.
Derive an enforceable sufficient condition for ellipticity and assess accuracy–robustness trade-offs.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses multiaxial experimental data from carbon black-filled EPDM rubber with varying curative contents to compare prediction accuracy and calibration robustness.
watch_item: Performance beyond the tested formulations and loading conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Constrained neural softening functions for the Mullins effect in parameter-dependent materials
